text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.1% today as refiners benefited from a day of mixed signals on diesel supply and pricing. Oil prices fell on news that the IEA (the International Energy Agency—a group of major oil-consuming countries) agreed to release diesel from strategic stockpiles to ease a global shortage, which typically helps refiner margins. However, the same day brought evidence that diesel remains genuinely tight: shipping costs from the Gulf to China hit $76 million per tanker (ten times pre-war levels), heating oil prices are soaring with Northeast households facing 21% higher winter bills, and the White House is under political pressure to act on fuel costs ahead of midterm elections in a month.

The two-week 13.7% surge reflects a broader shift in refiner economics: while oil prices have moderated recently thanks to emergency stockpile releases, the extreme tightness in diesel supply means refiners can still capture strong margins by producing it. The geopolitical backdrop—tanker attacks in the Persian Gulf and Iran's moves to disrupt shipping—keeps upside volatility in place, even as some relief measures (like the G7 release) have started to ease the immediate crisis.
